title: Conventionality in the Perspective of the Popular Responses of the Zulliger Test and the Personality Trait Openness to Experience
abstract: Abstract: Conventionality represents a key aspect of behavior in social contexts and can be assessed through the Openness to Experience trait or by popular (P) responses in performance-based methods such as the Rorschach Test. Although the Rorschach’s validity for assessing conventionality is well established, comparable evidence for the Zulliger Test is lacking. This study aimed to identify P responses on the Zulliger Test and examine their concurrent validity with socially adaptive conventionality, defined as the relationship between the frequency of popular responses and informant-rated Openness to Experience. Two studies were conducted with samples of 100 and 73 participants. Study 1 produced an updated list of P responses for the Zulliger Test; Study 2 replicated and validated these findings. Informant ratings of Openness were related to P-response frequency, and the association followed an inverted U-shaped pattern. Participants with a moderate P response frequency were described as more open to experience than those with low or very high frequencies. These findings support the conclusion that the Zulliger Test captures aspects of conventionality similar to those reflected in the Rorschach, underscoring its potential for assessing socially adaptive and maladaptive forms of (un)conventional behavior.
